questions.q: A customer_id column is stored as int64 in pandas. What is the right way to think about it?
options: It is a ratio variable, so its mean is useful
It is really a nominal label, so its mean is meaningless
It is continuous because it is a number
It is ordinal because bigger IDs are newer
questions.explain: An ID identifies a customer; arithmetic on it has no real-world meaning, even though pandas stores it as an integer.

Region
Order amount in dollars
Number of children in a household

questions.q: Why is temperature in Celsius an interval scale rather than a ratio scale?
options: Because its gaps are unequal
Because it cannot be measured precisely
Because zero is arbitrary, so 20 degrees is not 'twice as hot' as 10 degrees
Because it is categorical
questions.explain: Interval scales have equal gaps but no true zero, so ratios are not meaningful.

questions.q: Satisfaction ratings of low, medium and high are best classified as:
options: Nominal
Ordinal
Interval
Ratio
questions.explain: The labels have a natural order, but the distances between them are unknown.

questions.q: What does pd.Categorical(..., categories=[...], ordered=True) accomplish for a satisfaction column?
options: It converts the labels to random numbers
It lets max(), min() and sorting follow low < medium < high instead of alphabetical order
It turns the column into a ratio variable
It removes duplicate rows
questions.explain: Declaring an ordered categorical tells pandas the meaningful ranking of the labels.
